newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs close weak.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit down, hogs close weak.

text.p: CME pork belly futures remained locked down the daily limit of 2.000 cents per lb in all months at the close while hog futures also fell late to close lower to sharply lower, traders said.
February bellies closed limit down at 74.975 cents -- 2-1/2 month lows.

Carryover sell stops weighed on pork bellies from the start and futures punched through last week's lows at 75.175 cents to touch off further sell stops, pulling futures down early in the session. Technical and fundamental pressure combined to push prices lower, traders said.
"Technically, the (belly futures) market looks like a wreck," one trader said.
Traders also cited the stepped-up slaughter pace last week which weighed on the cash belly market. Hog runs and kills are too large for current demand, they said.
Cargill Investor Services sold early and E.D.&F. Man and LIT division of First Options notably sold on the break, pit sources said.

Hog futures also fell after ranging mixed early as spillover weakness from pork bellies and live cattle futures weighed on prices. Profit taking pulled futures into technical sell stops, especially in December, before short covering lightly pared losses at the close, they said.

Local buying prompted by steady to mostly higher cash hog markets had boosted prices to technical resistance early. But demand lacked follow through as cash indications turned mixed for Tuesday and the other pits moved lower. The market then turned technically weak when locals sold following the break in live cattle futures, they added.
"Charts point to 51 (cents) in December," said Julia Bussie, analyst for AG Edwards.

RBH notably sold while Rand Financials turned seller after buying early, traders said. Merrill Lynch and R.J. O'Brien also sold nearbys early while Iowa Grain sold February. Fund selling added to losses late, pit sources said.
In hog options, there was offering of December 56 to 58 calls early and offering of February 70 pits by R.J. O'Brien late, but trading remained light, pit sources added.
